subject: Order Form: Maintenance window wording and tiered service credit proposal
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novatech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novatech Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — maintenance windows / credits clarification

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the updated order form. A few follow-ups from procurement and ops:

1) Maintenance windows — we need clearer definition of what counts as an "operational maintenance" vs. "emergency maintenance" and whether planned windows are excluded from uptime calculations.

2) Service credits — procurement would like a laddered credit table (not single cap) tied to monthly uptime percentage. Also asking for a per-incident cap versus monthly cap.

3) Response times — could you confirm escalation times for P1/P2 in the Dedicated plan? They want guaranteed acknowledgement within 15 minutes for P1s.

We attached our preferred example table for reference. Happy to jump on a call if easier.

Best,
Eleanor
Eleanor Park
Head of IT Procurement
Novatech Systems

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — maintenance windows / credits clarification

Eleanor — thanks for the clear notes. Quick summary of what we can do and open items: 

- Maintenance classification: propose adding an explicit section that defines Planned Maintenance (scheduled >72 hours notice; excluded from uptime), Operational Maintenance (short rolling patches; excluded up to 2 hours/month), and Emergency Maintenance (security/incident-driven; excluded but triggers 1-for-1 rollback window).

- Credit ladder: we can adopt a tiered monthly credit schedule that scales by uptime bands (e.g., >=99.95%: 0 credits; 99.5–99.95%: 5% monthly credit; 99.0–99.5%: 15%; <99.0%: 30%), with a monthly cap of 50% of the monthly committed fee. We prefer a monthly cap to avoid unlimited per-incident exposure.

- Response times: our Dedicated plan SLA currently guarantees P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes and a targeted mitigation path within 1 hour. We can consider 15-minute acknowledgement if Novatech commits to a 12-month reserved capacity level (this is operationally required for guaranteed pager coverage).

I attached an editable redline of the order form (orderform_v2_redline.pdf) and a draft SLA matrix. Marissa/legal and Karthik/ops are on copy to weigh in on caps and operational feasibility.

Would you prefer we mark the order form with the three maintenance categories above or fold Operational into Planned?

Thanks,
Soojin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachment: orderform_v2_redline.pdf (pdf); support_sla_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novatech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — maintenance windows / credits clarification

Team / Eleanor — tagging legal perspectives. A few redline asks from legal: 

1) Cap mechanics — we can agree to a tiered credit ladder but legal wants a clear definition of how credits are calculated (pro-rata on the monthly recurring charge), how they are paid (invoice credit vs cash), and an absolute aggregate cap (we propose 50% monthly, 200% annual).

2) Exclusions — explicitly enumerate third-party outages, customer misconfiguration, and force majeure as exclusions from uptime calculations. Also add a procedure for Novatech to submit a credit claim within 30 days of the month in question, with required evidence (incident id, timestamps).

3) Maintenance notice windows — legal is fine with Planned (>72hrs) vs Emergency, but wants Operational Maintenance defined conservatively (we should allow up to 4 rolling hours/month to be excluded, not more).

4) Response SLOs — we can concede to 15-minute P1 acknowledgement only if the reserved capacity commit and a joint oncall roster are added to the Order Form. Otherwise we retain 30-min P1 acknowledgement.

I'll attach a redline PDF with tracked changes (orderform_v2_redline.pdf). If procurement asks for per-incident cash payouts, we should push back to invoice credits only.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novatech.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — maintenance windows / credits clarification

Operational notes from infra/ops: 

- To reliably support a 15-minute P1 ack we need a committed pool (reserved GPUs) plus a 24/7 primary/secondary oncall schedule with on-call handoffs in the Order Form. Otherwise our standard cadence is 30-minute ack with accelerated mitigation windows for high-severity incidents.

- Maintenance windows: we can mark Operational Maintenance as 'scheduled micro-patches' up to 2 hours/month where we don't cascade credits. If Novatech wants 0-hours considered, that will require a different service tier and changes to our rolling deploy process (higher cost).

- Credit measurement: we use region-level availability metrics aggregated per calendar month; we'll provide the metric export as part of the monthly SLA report (CSV). Ops prefers that credits be applied as invoice adjustments, not cash payouts — easier for bookkeeping.

Happy to walk through a short runbook during the next call.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novatech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft — maintenance windows / credits clarification

Thanks — this is helpful and much clearer. A couple quick confirmations so procurement can move to approval: 

• We accept a tiered monthly credit ladder with a 50% monthly cap and 200% annual aggregate cap as you proposed.
• Novatech will review the reserved capacity proposal internally; we aim to commit to a 12-month reserved tier if you can document the oncall roster and the changed ack SLA in the Order Form.
• We prefer invoice credits (not cash).

Can you please send a final clean order form + tracked redline and a DocuSign-ready packet? If you can get that to us by EOD Thursday we can route to legal and procurement and aim to sign next week.

Eleanor
--
